pl-l4d43c5-d1e115.summary: Asks whether the elect will then remember past evils as well as goods.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e118.summary: Notes that some authorities seem to teach that the good will not remember past evils, sins or torments.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e121.summary: Cites Isaiah: I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things will not be remembered nor come to mind, but you will rejoice forever.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e128.summary: Adds Isaiah, 'former distresses are forgotten', with Jerome: former evils will be forgotten, since perhaps in the future the memory of the old life will be wholly deleted as eternal goods succeed, lest remembering former distress be part of evil.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e140.summary: Interprets these as not excluding memory of past evils but removing from it distress and harm: their memory will not sadden the saints or darken their bliss, but make them more grateful to God.
claims: The blessed remember past evils without pain.
That memory makes them more grateful.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e143.summary: Cites Gregory on Psalm 88: how does one sing God's mercies forever who does not remember misery? But how is bliss full if the memory of guilt touches the mind? Yet often the joyful remember sad things without pain, and are more joyful and grateful for it.
claims: Joyful memory of past sorrow increases gratitude.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e155.summary: Concludes that if the saints remember former evils in the future, it will be not for punishment or diminishment of glory but for thanksgiving.
claims: Memory of evil serves thanksgiving in heaven.

pl-l4d43c5-d1e158.summary: Answers whether the elect's sins will then be known to all as the damned's evils will be: Scripture does not say so expressly; it may not unreasonably be thought that sins covered and deleted here by penance will there also be covered from others, while others are revealed to all.
claims: Sins covered by penance may remain hidden at the judgment.

pl-l4d43c5.summary: Asks whether the elect will remember past evils as well as goods. Isaiah and Jerome seem to say former evils will be forgotten; but these can be understood to remove not the memory but its sting, so that it does not sadden the saints but makes them more grateful, as Gregory asks how one can sing God's mercies forever without remembering misery. Whether the elect's sins will be known to all as the damned's are, Scripture does not say; it is not unreasonable to think sins covered by penance here will be covered there, others revealed.
claims: The blessed will remember past evils without pain.
Sins covered by penance may remain hidden at the judgment.
